subject: Post-call: Operational resilience & fallback options (FinVault)
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finvault.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Operational resilience & fallback options (FinVault)

Sam — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply with corrections/additions.

Summary of pain points (as discussed)
- Recent availability incidents causing SLO misses during capacity spikes.
- Long-tail latencies on larger prompts that cause timeouts for user-facing flows.
- Need for a deterministic graceful degradation path (smaller model / cached responses) rather than full outage.
- Auditability: fine-grained request logs and KV-cache persistence required for post-incident analysis.

Current stack (from you)
- Self-hosted model endpoints on GCP with autoscaling groups.
- Redis for short-lived session state; object storage for checkpoints.
- Internal routing that pins heavy workloads to a small pool to control cost.

Success criteria you shared
- SLO: p95 < 200ms for conversational back-end in steady state; p99 targets to be discussed.
- Graceful degrade flow that keeps read-only flows available using a quantized fallback model.
- Cross-region failover within ~90s for catastrophic region outages.
- KMS integration for any persisted user artifacts; no token retention beyond what is required.

Incident history (high-level)
- You mentioned three incidents last quarter: two capacity spikes during batch jobs and one OOM while handling long-context requests. We captured these in the incident timeline you sent and will use that to validate runbook assumptions.

Our initial recommendation / next steps
1) I attached a lightweight resilience_matrix.xlsx and our SOC2-summary.pdf for your security folks.
2) Technical deep-dive with Redwood infra + your platform ops (60–90m) — proposed week of Dec 6.
3) Pilot configuration: Dedicated reserved pool sized for peak QPS + automatic prefix/KV cache enabled; fallback model policy (10% canary to start) and cross-region standby.
4) Draft runbook & pricing ballpark from us after the deep-dive; we’ll include cost implications for reserved capacity vs. burst.

Please confirm: 1) the SLO targets above match what you expect to evaluate on the pilot, and 2) who from your infra team should be on the deep-dive call.

Thanks — happy to adjust if I missed anything.

— Evelyn Hart
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: resilience_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: SOC2-summary.pdf (pdf)]
From: Sam Torres <sam.torres@finvault.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, FinVault Platform Team <platform@finvault.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Operational resilience & fallback options (FinVault)

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. That aligns well. A few clarifications and additional asks from our side:

Confirmations
- SLO targets: p95 < 200ms is our initial gating criteria for user flows. For background jobs we can accept higher tail latency but want notification thresholds.
- Graceful degrade: yes — fallback must preserve safety filters and customer-specific prompt pre/post processing.

Additional info / asks
- Incidents: attaching a short incident_timeline.csv with timestamps and root causes. Two incidents were autoscaler-related (spike due to batch infer jobs) and one was an OOM after a 50k-token prompt.
- Audit & retention: we need request-level auditing for at least 90 days and KMS integration for any persisted KV entries.
- Security: please confirm SOC2 scope for private deployments vs hosted.
- Cost: please include a rough monthly estimate for a Dedicated reserved pool (3x nominal production capacity) and an estimate for burst/overage.

Next steps from FinVault
- I’ll bring our infra lead (Maya Rao) onto the technical deep-dive if we confirm Dec 8 or Dec 9.
- We’ll share the internal runbook excerpts prior to the call.

Attached: incident_timeline.csv (short csv)

Thanks,
Sam Torres
Head of Platform — FinVault
[Attachment: incident_timeline.csv (csv)]

- Confirm availability for deep-dive on Dec 8 (Evelyn pls confirm) — include infra ops + security (SOC2 owner).
- Marissa action: compile fallback model options (gpt-small-ptq, gpt-medium-8bit) and brief perf/latency tradeoffs — deliverable by Dec 3.

Also: we should prepare a one-page customer-facing runbook excerpt to show during the next call (calls out failover times, expected degraded latency, and observable signals).
